info.title: sLaunch
info.author: etonedemid
info.details: sLaunch is a fast text based HOME menu replacement inspired by niagara launcher.

changelog:
v0.8.0
The cross-media bar comes to sLaunch. New XMB mode (Theming > UI mode) does the PSP thing properly: categories ride a bar across the screen, your games hang below the selected one, and the whole thing is touch-driven - tap a category to open it, drag the column to flick through, tap an entry twice to launch.

Two long-standing annoyances are gone. Closing a homebrew now brings you back to the menu instead of relaunching the homebrew forever, and Restart / Power off now actually restart and power off instead of leaving the console in a weird half-asleep state.

Icon packs are in: drop PNG sets into slaunch/icon_packs// and switch between them in Theming > Icon pack. A clean Minimal pack by @meepcat55 ships in the box. Themes also gained an icon background colour, so packs sit right on any look.

sLaunch now speaks Russian, Japanese, German, Spanish and Chinese - it follows your console's language automatically, and slaunch/lang/template.txt is there if you want to add yours. Korean and Chinese consoles get their proper system font too, and a full Noto Sans CJK is bundled under Theming > Fonts.

Also: dragging anywhere now moves the content under your finger (not the cursor), taps in submenus land where you actually tap, and the welcome screen slimmed down to a quiet two lines that fade in and out.

Install:- run sInstaller.nro, or extract slaunch-v0.8.0-sd.zip to your SD root. Reboot after.

v0.7.0
sLaunch now says hello. On boot (and right after setup) you get a welcome screen that greets you by your Switch profile name over the opening jingle, with a different line each time. Don't want it? Theming > Welcome screen.

You can also clean up the menu now - every system entry (Album, Browser, Settings, Power, Homebrew...) can be shown or hidden in Theming > Menu entries. Theming itself stays put so you can always get back.

New Random game entry: it rolls through your library like a slot machine, lands on something, and launches it.

Setup got restyled to match the rest of the menu instead of looking like its own thing.
